messages.content: 計算在投擲100次硬幣，每次獲得正面的機率為0.5的情況下，觀察到60次正面的機率。

function.name: calc_binomial_prob
function.description: Calculates the probability of an outcome based on the binomial distribution Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

num_success.description: Number of times the event of interest has occurred.

prob_success.description: Probability of the event of interest on any single experiment. This is a float type value.

message.reasoning:
The user asks in Chinese: "計算在投擲100次硬幣，每次獲得正面的機率為0.5的情況下，觀察到60次正面的機率。" They want the probability of observing 60 heads out of 100 flips with p=0.5. That's binomial probability: C(100,60)*(0.5)^60*(0.5)^40 = C(100,60)*0.5^100. We can compute numeric value. Use function calc_binomial_prob. Provide result. Let's compute approximate. C(100,60) = 100 choose 60 = 100 choose 40. That is large. Let's approximate using Python? We can approximate manually: 100 choose 60 = 100!/(60!40!). We can compute log. But maybe we can give exact expression and approximate decimal. Let's approximate using known values: 100 choose 50 ~ 1.0089e29. 100 choose 40 ~ 1.0089e28? Actually 100 choose 40 = 100 choose 60. Let's compute approximate: Using known binomial coefficient values: 100 choose 40 = 100 choose 60 = 100!/(40!60!). I can approximate using logs: log10(100!) ~ 157.97. log10(40!) ~ 47.51. log10(60!) ~ 81.58. Sum of denominators logs = 129.09. So log10(C) = 157.97 - 129.09 = 28.88. So C ~ 7.6e28? Actually 10^28.88 = 7.6e28. Then multiply by 0.5^100 = 7.888609e-31? Wait 0.5^100 = 7.888609e-31. Multiply: 7.6e28 * 7.8886e-31 = 7.6*7.8886 e(-2) = 59.9e-2 = 0.599. That seems too high. Actually probability of exactly 60 heads out of 100 with p=0.5 is about 0.028? Wait typical distribution: mean 50, sd sqrt(25)=5. So 60 is 2 sd above mean. Probability of exactly 60 is around 0.028? Let's compute more accurately: Use binomial probability formula: C(100,60)*0.5^100. Let's compute C(100,60). Use known value: 100 choose 60 = 100 choose 40 = 100!/(40!60!). I can compute using known values: 100 choose 40 = 100 choose 60 = 100 choose 40. Let's compute using Python mentally? Might be easier to use approximate: Use normal approximation: P(X=60) ≈ (1/(sqrt(2πnpq))) * exp(-(k-np)^2/(2npq)). Here n=100, p=0.5, q=0.5, npq=25. So sqrt(2π*25)= sqrt(157.08)=12.53. So probability mass at k=60: exp(-(10)^2/(50))=exp(-100/50)=exp(-2)=0.1353. So approximate probability = 1/12.53 * 0.1353 = 0.0108. That seems plausible. Actually exact probability is about 0.028? Let's compute more precisely: Use binomial coefficient: 100 choose 60 = 100 choose 40. Let's compute using known values: 100 choose 40 = 100 choose 60. I can compute using product: C(100,40) = product_{i=1}^{40} (100+1-i)/i. Let's approximate quickly: Use log: ln(C) = sum_{i=1}^{40} [ln(100+1-i) - ln(i)]. Compute approximate using known values?
